sense.text:
Jeremiah is speaking of the plight of Israel in his day: “Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!” He felt in his spirit the calamities coming on our people, and he wished he could cry all day for the slain of his people.

That empathy is normal. We are supposed to feel that way for our people: they are our own flesh and blood, descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. When a mother has to watch the man who killed her son Cyrus Belton walk free, when our brother Nolan Wells goes out on a simple boat ride with Edomites he took for friends, who are not our friends, and never makes it back home, when Carmelo Anthony gets 35 years for self-defense, the heart of Israel goes out to them. But there is a balance to it. We still have to stay in the spirit.

precepts.why:
“For death is come up into our windows, and is entered into our palaces, to cut off the children from without, and the young men from the streets.” Every time we turn on the news, the television, social media, all we see is our people being put to death: police killings, lynchings, deaths left unsolved. Sandra Bland, Tamir Rice, Eric Garner; the list goes on and on.

We cannot escape it. Sometimes it hits close to home, and our own loved ones are put to death. The children are cut off and the young men from the streets: our people are dropping like flies. That is why the prophet wept for the slain of the daughter of his people.

The prophets of old had the same heart, but look at how they moved. “Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people.” Hands up, don’t shoot; unarmed; houses busted into with no search warrant; ICE out collecting our people, some of them citizens, carried off to foreign places. It is natural for repenting Israelites caught up in the midst of this to feel for our people in the world who are being mistreated.

“Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission, Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.” Non-stop crying for our people, but he understood that this thing is of the Lord, and he had to wait on the Lord: he would cry until the Lord looked down.

So we cannot take matters into our own hands, or join and attach ourselves to certain causes prematurely. We have to be very mindful.

“For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt”: for the pain and suffering of his people, the prophet himself was hurt. As a prophet and as an Israelite, we are going to feel attachment, compassion, sympathy and empathy for our people when they are put to death, mistreated, wrongfully incarcerated, or given 35 years for self-defense. It is natural to do so. If you don’t feel some type of way about our people being put to death left and right, something is wrong with you.

“Now therefore, Lord, I will speak; touching man in general, thou knowest best; but touching thy people, for whose sake I am sorry.” Ezra is not concerned with all the races of people. When it comes to man in general, the Most High knows best: he has a will for Moab, a will for Ammon, a will for Ishmael. But for his people, Ezra is sorry.

“And for thine inheritance, for whose cause I mourn; and for Israel, for whom I am heavy; and for Jacob, for whose sake I am troubled.” He mourns only for God’s inheritance, Israel, the seed of Jacob.

So it is with us. The racial tension now is so thick you could cut it with a knife; the workplace with Jake and Esau is not the same; people are walking on eggshells, and other nations are discussing what is going on in the US. If you are watching the news and keeping up with what is happening to our people, how we are abused and used in this society, you are going to be heavy and troubled, just as it is written.

sense.text: The Pharisees and Sadducees came tempting Christ for a sign from heaven, and he answered, “When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red.” Jake always thinks he is a meteorologist; we just stick a hand out the window and say it is going to be nice today.

“O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?” You can predict the weather, but you cannot line up what is going on: you do not see what time we are living in, that we are in the latter days, that prophecy is being fulfilled. All of us should be able to discern the signs of the times.

precepts.why: “Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation.” We should not be living under a rock or be clueless. We should know what is going on around us and be up to speed with current events, not only in Babylon but all around the world, because our people are scattered to the four corners of the earth. Our forefathers kept up with what was going on, and they were able to line those things up with the scriptures.

“In the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” The books are the scriptures, the prophecies. Daniel matched the current events of his time with what was written, and saw that he was living in the time Jeremiah spoke of in Jeremiah 29.

If you are not watching and praying, how can you line up what is going on today with the scriptures and know how to move in wisdom?

“And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes.” Once he understood the time, he sought after God, knowing everything is of God’s divine will and counsel. It may seem chaotic, as if things are happening spontaneously all over the place, but we are never outside of God’s program, and this is not our rest.

sense.text:
“This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.” Perilous means danger: full of hazard and uncertainty. We are living in perilous times right now. Lynchings, our bodies found hanging from trees, a lot of racial anger and tension, and we as repenting Israelites rehearsing the righteous acts are surrounded by danger and controversy. So we have to have the mind of a soldier and the mind of a judge.

You must know this. When we read the Bible and then see what happened to Cyrus Belton, chased 120 yards (that is not self-defense), we can line it up: it is going to be hardship. This is not our kingdom. We are prisoners of war, the other nations hate our guts, and there is no constitution made for us. We cannot get caught up in it; we have to stay level-headed.

precepts.why:
If we read the prophets we understand the climate we are living in, and we will not be shocked. I can’t stand when a negro is shocked: why are they treating us this way? That is your enemy. What are you talking about? Did you forget how you arrived? It wasn’t on a yacht. It wasn’t first class, negro.

“And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron”: the fourth kingdom is Rome. “And whereas thou sawest the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided.” The feet and toes, the last part of the fourth beast, are the EU and America, the time period we are living in.

The kingdom shall be divided: that is racial tension, and there is always going to be racial tension, as it is written. “So the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.” America is strong militarily, but broken and divided, because America made a big melting pot. God says no: there are two manner of people and they shall be separated. Within Esau there is a perpetual hatred for us, within Moab a hatred, within Ishmael a hatred. All nations hate our guts.

So a hot racial climate, controversy all over the place, lynchings in 2026 that they call suicides, all of it is this time period the Bible spoke of. And it is normal for us to feel connected to our people lost in the world, but we still have to keep the mind of Christ in all things.

sense.text:
When Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned to Jerusalem, Jehu the son of Hanani the seer met him and said, “Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord.”

The Lord does not like that. When Rodney Hinton was accused of killing a sheriff’s deputy with his car the day after police killed his son, our people cheered him as he walked through the courtroom. But hear the whole matter: his son Ryan was one of four fleeing a stolen car, armed with a gun stolen from a woman, and allegedly pointed it at the police. That boy was not innocent. If we had shown up ten thousand deep in purple and gold for that, we would not be just.

We are soldiers, and a soldier hates to see one of his own fall, but we are judges at the same time. We have to be careful not to bring wrath on ourselves and on the congregation.

precepts.why:
“And after this did Jehoshaphat king of Judah join himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who did very wickedly.” What we just saw in that article was a case of our people doing very wickedly and the powers that be being a terror to them; Romans 13 played itself out.

“Because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the Lord hath broken thy works. And the ships were broken, that they were not able to go to Tarshish.” We are doing mighty works, all praises for good leadership, for our bishops and our deacons, and for those who labor in Christ before us. But if we join ourselves with those who do wickedly, the Lord will break our works.

We are not saying this kingdom is just at all. It is scrapping everything given with the Civil Rights Act; the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act so that majority black districts are cracked to pieces and whites stay in power. This whole system is corrupt as hell and designed against our people. We are in the belly of the beast, Babylon the Great. But as we can see that, we can also see when our people are wrong and doing wickedness.

sense.text:
They are firing everybody as DEI hires, when the truth is DEI mostly benefits white women, the real DEI hires, while blacks have to be overqualified and overexperienced and do twice as good as their white and Asian counterparts just to get the job, and they are the ones losing it. They want to scrap affirmative action and EBT. All of it is because this whole country, this whole system, is built off of our bloodshed and our suffering: we are the fuel that keeps it running, our blood and our bones.

But nothing we are discussing is outside of God’s will or plan. God does not want us comfortable, or having a majority vote in Memphis or anywhere, because then the slave starts getting comfortable and does not want to be free any more.

“Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest.” The American dream is not for you or for me. That does not mean don’t go to school or better yourself, get your degree, make a better life for your wife and children. But God does not want us thinking for one second that this is our kingdom. Our minds cannot comprehend what God has in store for the Israelites who wait for him.

“Because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction.” The whole system is polluted from the very foundation: they were writing that all men are created equal while we were in the cotton field: beyond hypocrisy, beyond devilish. The whole thing is designed to destroy our people. When our people think they can circumvent God and make their way in America, in politics, as a Herodian, God says no: it will destroy you with a sore destruction.

precepts.why:
“Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” The throne of iniquity is America, Babylon the Great, the ruler of all kingdoms. There are many smaller thrones of iniquity throughout Europe and the Arab countries where we are scattered (Afro-Turks, Afro-Syrians, Afro-Iraqis), but this is the big throne of iniquity right here.

They frame mischief by a law: executive, legislative, judicial, every branch is designed to target our people. That is why the laws and the penalties fall on what happens in urban communities, ghettos and inner cities, all the dog-whistle terms for where we dwell. The Lord God is giving the whole system a negro wake-up call, black and brown alike, even the ones telling the ICE agent they are not black. We keep this in mind, but at the same time we must keep the mind of a judge.

sense.text: God is calling us as Israelites, especially the men, to be judges. “Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates”, “and they shall judge the people with just judgment.” We cannot be blind, and we cannot be soldiers without discipline: a soldier without biblical education is nothing more than a criminal with power. That biblical education is what makes a soldier wise and understanding, able to discern matters, wise as a serpent and harmless as a dove: a judge.

“Thou shalt not wrest judgment; thou shalt not respect persons.” It is easy to overlook the wickedness of our people and side with them just because they are our people. Our heart goes out to our brothers being killed, but God says thou shalt not respect persons in judgment.

As a judge we must stay level-headed. We cannot lay hands on any man suddenly or join hand in hand with every cause, lest we bring evil on ourselves and the Lord break our works, as with Jehoshaphat.

precepts.why:
“My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change.” Fear the Lord and the king means respect the powers that be and fear God. Meddle not with them that are given to change: our people in the world stand with us one day and the next they are celebrating Christmas, Thanksgiving, birthdays and the Fourth of July. One minute they want to be revolutionaries, the next they are speaking evil of us and gainsaying everything we stand for. As soon as the World Cup comes, Jake gets distracted. They are simple as hell.

“For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?” Calamity is coming on them, so don’t meddle or get caught up with them.

“These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.” There it is again: the wise judge does not respect persons.

Jehoshaphat “set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city”: judges are soldiers with a biblical education.

“Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment.” It is very easy to get caught up in popular persuasion and controversy, even among our own people, but we judge for the Lord.

“Wherefore now let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.” Take heed and do what the Bible says. There is no iniquity with our God, so we cannot join ourselves to iniquity either, and God does not respect persons.

sense.text: “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”: the rod is Christ, and the Branch is the Messiah. Here we examine the mind of Christ, the mind of the judge we have to follow.
“The spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord” rests on him.

“And shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”: when you study the scriptures and get your biblical education, it makes you of quick understanding.

“And he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears.” When that father walked through the courtroom, there were mixed emotions. But Christ does not judge by what he sees or hears at first. We cannot be quick to speak on matters; sometimes we have to let it play itself out before we join ourselves to a cause, lest we be found guilty and God has to deal with us.

“But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” We think equity is the money from owning a house, but equity is fairness or justice in the way people are treated, free of disparities between races and the like. We have to do everything with equity: fair and with justice.

precepts.why:
The Lord left us an example, with no emotion, and we follow in Christ’s steps: “Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.” We are sensationalized by the news: black person killed, black person missing, black person found hanging from a tree. We are so shell-shocked that the moment we see anything happen to our people we go straight on the defense.

We have to let the whole thing play itself out, and have a full understanding of everything before we speak on a matter or align ourselves with any cause or protest.

Keep a pragmatic mindset: dealing with the problems of a specific situation in a reasonable and logical way, not an emotional one, instead of going by ideas, theories and our own opinions; practical as opposed to idealistic. That is how a good judge has to be.

“Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.” Our opinions, ideas and feelings do not work the righteousness of God. These things that are happening are not outside of God’s program, so we have to be very mindful and not get caught up.

“Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.” Black people love jumping to conclusions: three minutes into a movie we already know who the bad guy is. Understand first.

“Answer not before thou hast heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talk.” Don’t speak on a matter until you have heard the full cause; sometimes it is more than what the eye can see.

“Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.” “My son, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent.” That is Jehoshaphat again: meddle much, and God will have to deal with us too. “And if thou follow after, thou shalt not obtain, neither shalt thou escape by fleeing.”

“He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.” To answer a matter before hearing the whole of it is foolishness, and we cannot bring shame on the ministry or engage in foolishness.

“Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?” The law does not judge any man before it hears the whole matter and knows all his doings. We have been trained throughout the scriptures to hear the whole conclusion.

Our forefathers were excellent judges: Daniel made diligent inquisition in the days of Susanna, and King Solomon judged between the two women, one whose child had died and one whose child was alive. Many examples in the scriptures show our forefathers discerning between good and evil, right and wrong.
“The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.” We cannot be simple, believing every word. The prudent man looks well to his goings, and that is how we have to be.

“A wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.” Time matters because sometimes you need time to think on a matter properly, and time for things to play themselves out.

That is why a court case has discovery: evidence that was not seen when probable cause was first found is brought forth, and the case goes from alleged to proven innocent or proven guilty. A wise man discerns both time and judgment.

“It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.” God hides matters, situations and wisdom; the honour of a king is to get to the bottom of something, examine all the facts and leave no stone unturned.

And as we search, we must remember God’s divine will for our people, the big picture.

sense.text: “They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.” Most of our people in the world worship a strange god, whether Cesare Borgia, the image of the white man, or a rock in Mecca. With abominations every day: the LGBTQ community, all manner of unclean foods, birthdays, Christmas and Thanksgiving.
“They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up.”
“Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.” Christ is our Rock, capital R. Our people don’t give a damn about this Bible or this truth.
“And when the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters.” The Lord saw the mind of our people and the evil in our communities, and he abhorred it.

“And he said, I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” We are reading God’s program and living in God’s program. The white man is not operating outside of God’s program. Our people are caught up in all manner of evil and wickedness, with no faith, and God has hidden his face.

precepts.why:
“I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” Our people are caught up in many offences right now, and God says he is going back to his place: he is not defending them, and we cannot defend them either.

Our people are hardheaded, rebellious knuckleheads, and it takes things hitting home before they start to seek God. Death has to come up into our windows, as we read in Jeremiah 9.

“When he slew them, then they sought him.” When he puts us to death, then we want to seek after God. It takes all that: we are a stiff-necked and hardheaded people. Whether by an officer, the Klan or random white folks (ask Zimmerman; you can’t even walk with a hoodie on), we cannot even hear God until he starts shaking up our lives and putting us to death. We are dropping like flies, and that is God’s program.

“He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.” Until we are oppressed our ears are not even open. Our ears are open to Megan Thee Stallion and Cardi B, and a song about stealing, boosting and robbing folks is the number one hit in the US, but they are closed to God’s word and to the prophets. So God opens our ears in oppression.

Many of our people are going to repent behind what happened to Cyrus Belton and to Carmelo Anthony, because they will realize that the brothers in purple were saying that our enemies would slay us and hold themselves not guilty. Many will come to repentance behind God’s judgment on our neighborhoods.

God knows how to make Israel listen. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen.” We are the majority on this earth, but scattered among all the nations and left few in number among them: that is why they call us minorities.

“And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone”: Cesare Borgia, the work of the hands of Leonardo da Vinci; Christianity.

“But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul. When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days.” That is the time we are in now, when our people are lynched left and right, when a boat ride or an elevator full of white folks can be your last. We are living in perilous times.

sense.text: Oppression makes a wise man mad, and it does, but we have to behave wisely and not live in our emotions. “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.” That is our job: a watchman for our people, those in the truth and those outside it.

“When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.” Our job is to warn the wicked, because if you sin, the judgment comes. A lot of times our people die and are caught in calamities because of sin. We speak to save their life, and that is why you see purple and gold everywhere you go: we don’t want their blood on our hands, so we teach the gospel: leave sin, flee sin.

“Yet if thou warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul.” A lot of our people die in their iniquities. They love the white Jesus, and when you tell them to stop sinning they curse you out. It hurts us to see our people in such a condition, but it is all the Lord’s doing. Can a thing happen on the earth and the Lord not know about it?

precepts.why: “Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.” All souls are his, the righteous and those not keeping God’s laws. We have to know the scripture and see these things: it hurts, yes, but we have to see these things.

“For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord God.” We do not see these things with a happy heart, because we share the same blood and the same complexion: that is our brother, that is our sister, and it hurts us. But we have to move in wisdom.

“Wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.” That is what the Lord wants for all his people. Turn and live: that is all we have to do as a people.

sense.text:
“Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded.” We play our position as disciplined soldiers, soldiers with a biblical education; we cannot get caught up. Sober minded means don’t smoke weed and don’t be drunk, absolutely, but it also means keeping a clear head in every situation and possessing your soul.

Do we feel emotion? Yes, we proved that: the prophets always had a heart and compassion for their people. But as servants of God we have to move in the spirit of Christ, who was an austere man. Soldiers cannot be emotional.

precepts.why:
“Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” This whole world is dark and this whole system is corrupt.

So we walk in the whole armour of God, not with emotions, feelings or opinions, “that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.”

“Having your loins girt about with truth”, the loins of your mind, as Peter writes; “the breastplate of righteousness”; “your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace.” Everything we arm ourselves with is the word of God, the faith of God and the mission at hand. It did not say take your opinions and emotions with you.

“For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.” We walk in this flesh and have to make a living in this present world, but we cannot operate like those in the world. “For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.”

“Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God.” Our people imagine America has their best interest, that they can marry a white woman, that there is such a thing as having white friends. We love learning the hard way. We bring “every thought to the obedience of Christ”, with no emotions and none of our own opinions in our armour.

“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” We have to be ready to use these situations, these calamities and atrocities, especially when, after hearing the facts and the whole matter, our people turn out to be innocent: murdered or incarcerated unjustly, things planted on them. Those things do happen, and we have to be ready to use them to bring our people to Christ and teach them the gospel.

sense.text:
There will always be something, because this is not our rest. “Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us.” Judgment is far from our people. So we cannot be shocked when police do all manner of evil, use unreasonable force, say they feared for their life, and get off. If you are shocked, you don’t study. We don’t know what justice looks like.

“We wait for light, but behold obscurity”: we are always confused, and “we walk in darkness.”

“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes”: we grope thinking democracy will bring change, that maybe we should be Republicans, maybe liberals, as if any of it will make a difference. It won’t.

“We stumble at noonday as in the night”: the prophets are on the corner saying this is the way, but our people stumble as in the night. “We are in desolate places as dead men”: spiritually dead, the walking dead, in Babylon the Great and all the places we are scattered.

“We roar all like bears”: that is the civil unrest, hands up don’t shoot, black lives matter, say his name. “And mourn sore like doves”: that is the heart we must have for our people; we are always crying.

“We look for judgment, but there is none”: we look for judgment from a crooked system, and there is none for us. “For salvation, but it is far off from us”: someone to save us from our low state.

Why is all this happening? “For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us.” Our people are rotten, and wickedness is increasing on the earth. So there will always be controversy and civil unrest, whether people are innocent or guilty, and we have to use these highly controversial moments to edify our people, bring them to Christ and show them the right way.

Especially when our people are wronged, murdered or wrongly incarcerated, like Carmelo Anthony, Tamir Rice, Eric Garner, our brother George Floyd, we have to be right there to give our people an answer.

“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction”: adversity is oppression, and the water of affliction is our tears, mothers sobbing daily like the mother of our brother Cyrus Belton.

“Yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers.” When these things happen the teachers are not kept in a corner. There is a time and a place where we show up, as we did for our brother Kendrick Johnson, found rolled up in a gym mat. The purple army, that great army written in Ezekiel 37, will show up for our people and stand in solidarity, showing that we love and will defend our people. We are not making light of that: there is a time to assemble and speak with boldness about the evil done to our people, revealing who the enemy is and who the man of sin is.

“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it.” A word behind thee, because after something happens and we try to give our people the answer, many of them walk away from the truth. This is the way, you so-called blacks and Latinos, our people of the diaspora spread across the four corners of the earth: repent in Christ, keep the commandments, keep the laws. That is what will fix our broken people and our broken communities.

precepts.why:
“But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts”: nothing comes before God’s mission. We cannot let emotions fill our minds or cloud ourselves with anger and fury.

“And be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear.” We always have to be ready to give our people an answer, because many of them don’t understand what is happening to them. They want to go around God: they want prosperity without God in the equation.

“For the people turneth not unto him that smiteth them, neither do they seek the Lord of hosts.” Who is smiting our people? Our people don’t turn to him who is doing it. They turn to the white man: Mr. White Man, give us justice, give us freedom, give us our manhood, like it is sold on a shelf at Walmart.

Our eyes see the white man, but in the spirit we should know it is God who is allowing it and God who brought it on us. Our people are so simple they don’t turn to the one really doing the smiting, and that is why we must be ready always to give an answer.

“And it shall come to pass, when thou shalt shew this people all these words, and they shall say unto thee, Wherefore hath the Lord pronounced all this great evil against us? or what is our iniquity? or what is our sin that we have committed against the Lord our God?” When we stand on the corners and prophesy, and show them Zechariah 11, that their possessors slay them and hold themselves not guilty, and Isaiah, that we are going to be mass incarcerated, hidden in prison holes, they will say: I thought y’all said we were his chosen people. If we are so special, why all this evil?

“Then shalt thou say unto them, Because your fathers have forsaken me, saith the Lord, and have walked after other gods, and have served them, and have worshipped them, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my law.” Your mother taught you birthdays, your daddy taught you Christmas, your grandma taught you white Jesus, and you serve them with that cross around your neck. You don’t keep commandment one.

“And ye have done worse than your fathers; for, behold, ye walk every one after the imagination of his evil heart, that they may not hearken unto me.” That is the answer we give.

sense.text:
Christ was not emotional. He did not get caught up; he understood what was going on, that it is all part of the program. “Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people.” The Most High already gave us an example.

Christ is our commander. Commanders are not moved by emotion or easily swayed by what is going on. They think it through: they are strategic and calculated, they have contingencies in place, they understand that one thing creates another and dominoes fall, and they consider the end before they make any move. It ain’t checkers.
If Christ is our commander, that makes us soldiers. “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” We have to endure hardness as good soldiers.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life.” We are at war: spiritual war. We don’t use guns or weapons, but spiritual war is the most powerful mode of warfare. Our forefathers understood that in this gospel and this mission we are all soldiers on the battlefield; that is how Paul referred to his fellow labourers.

“That he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” To please God, who has called us to be soldiers, we cannot be entangled with the affairs of this life. If you are entangled with the affairs of this life, you want to please men. We have to be good soldiers with the mind of a judge, which comes from biblical education.

precepts.why:
“For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.” Our conversation is in heaven and we look for the Saviour, so we cannot be entangled with the affairs of this life.

What does God require of us? What is God’s mission? Gather the twelve tribes of Israel from the four corners of the earth; let the elect, the 144, be sealed, so we can go home.

We cannot be weak, soft, mushy and emotional; we are not choir boys. “This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare.” Brothers, we have to war a good warfare: not emotional, not caught up with the wicked, not striking hands with thieves and murderers and people stealing cars and guns and getting into shootouts with police, and muddying our good works.

“Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck.” Get caught up moving off of emotions, and you make shipwreck. We are all going to feel a certain type of way, with all that is going on and Nolan Wells missing, but we have to remember everything is of the Lord.

sense.text: Our God is not to be played with. “For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord.” God is going to pay back the wicked. “And again, The Lord shall judge his people.” That is what we always have to remember when we see all this death and get caught up: God will repay the heathen, and God is dealing with his people. Remember where judgment starts first.

precepts.why: “All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” We prophesy on the corners and warn our people that God’s judgment will come on them if they remain in their sins, and they say nothing is going to happen to us: here y’all go with that Bible again. But surely evil does come and overtake them. Many times when we prophesy at an event, after we leave the whole thing gets shot up: gunfire, stabbings, shootings.

Even we inside this truth are going to suffer. What happens to Jake in the world, wrongful incarceration, being murdered by police or by random blue-collar and white-collar heathen, will happen to us as well. But “let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” We will die in our innocence, in our faith and our righteousness, and we have to be very mindful not to be caught up as busybodies.

“Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.” We are not ashamed when we suffer, because there is a kingdom in store for us, and Christ will say well done, good and faithful servant.

“For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God.” The house of God is the nation of Israel. We see it in both kingdoms of the house of Israel: on our people in the streets, and in the medical industry, where the hospital is one of the most unsafe places for our women. We have been having babies since babies were babies, we were their mammies and raised their children, but now having a child is one of the most dangerous things a black woman can do. It was the same in Egypt; we see the eugenics agenda.

“And if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?” We see God dealing with us, so what shall the end of them be?

You sick of this place? God is too. “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” We have to tell our people to come out so they don’t get destroyed with this place. As long as there is breath in their body there is hope: they can repent. Repentance is for Israel and Israel only; the white man and the Arab man cannot be saved.

“For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.” Tamir Rice, Eric Garner, Mike Brown, Sandra Bland, Cyrus Belton, Martin Luther King, Patrice Lumumba, Emmett Till, Tulsa: how soon we forget, but God remembers all of it.

“Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works.” There is judgment in store for them. God showed us his face in the curses, and he does not play; what makes them think he will play with them?

“Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken.” The cup is the cup of God’s fury, Deuteronomy 28 and Leviticus 26. It was never God’s will for us to drink it or be under the hand of our enemies; he wanted us living in peace and safety in our own land, the kingdom of heaven on earth. But we have surely drunk of the cup, and we are still drinking it.

“And art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink of it.” That is what God says to these heathen, to the white man: they shall surely drink of God’s judgment and fury.

We are going to rejoice in that day. “Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them.” Edom used the legislative, judicial and executive branches to take vengeance; he weaponized the police, the original slave catchers, and ICE against us. Out of envy and hatred he revenged himself on us and did things unspeakable.

“I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it.” The white man loves his animals; Airbud has to go, and Lassie too.

“And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel: and they shall do in Edom according to mine anger and according to my fury.” It is written that way because we are soft: we have been conditioned to care for them, to help them up when they fall and hold the door for the old lady. God says no: he remembers the ships, the thousands slain, the lynchings, the cauldrons, and our forefather Nat Turner the prophet, whose skin they made into wallets and whose skull they drank wine out of.

The day is coming for righteous vengeance, but now is not that time. “And they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord God”: Esau, Ishmael, Moab and Ammon are all going to know God’s vengeance. We are not to take vengeance, and we are not to side with the wicked either.

“He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity”: the white man, the Arab man, all of them are going in chains. We built the great wall and the White House. They are still selling us on auction blocks in Mauritania and throughout North and Northeast Africa. “He that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword.”

“Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.” What we need as good soldiers and as good judges is patience, and we must keep our faith. We cannot stray from the mission or the protocol. We have to be just, as good soldiers and judges in these last days.
